correctness.rationale: For b≥1, a=2b+1 and sign(0)=+1, direct integer branch iteration establishes the two piecewise first-return formulas on disjoint blocks A_m≤x<A_(m+1). The proof checks nonnegative, negative and returning affine segments and their first-hit inequalities. Every plane point eventually crosses the nonnegative ray y=0; the inverse is explicit, so the return-cycle exhaustion implies all points periodic. The orbit decomposition consists of an O_m starting coordinate and b E_(m+1) plus b E_m entries, yielding return period 2b+1 and flight-time sum 4m(2b+1). Distinct O_m representatives give exactly m primitive plane cycles of each period. Independently direct-simulated returns and exact primitive planar periods for b=1..5, m≤12 are corroboration, not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: Only a=2b+1 for integer b≥1; no general two-parameter classification.
